en: The Old Master Wumen early on cultivated the dhūta practices; he subsequently studied Linji Chan. He traveled to fifteen monasteries, responding to conditions as they arose.
Eighty-four thousand verses flowed from his mouth into the profound mystery, encompassing the past and present and drawing the devotion of both clergy and laity.
His magnificent eloquence was penetrating.

The imperial hearing of the Ninefold Palace was moved by divine mechanism during three days of rain. Although the monastic robes were half-entranced by both faith and doubt, the court officials vied with one another to praise and replace him.
Who knows that this old fellow is like the great void, having forgotten both right and wrong—how could there be anger or joy?
He sports within the illusory samādhi, gathering in sentient beings who have the karmic affinity; his disciples’ mouths...
The transmission was entrusted to the attendant, who committed it to writing. Before the time for Nirvana had even arrived, the merit of the collective compilation was already accomplished.
He did not emulate the transformation at the Golden Land in the Bamboo Grove Monastery; he did not prize hanging his straw sandals upon the corner of the Dragon Bed;

he did not admire learning from the Ox-Head Mountain or entering meditative absorption in a stone chamber; nor did he envy those who, like the Lotus Sutra, spoke of paying homage while seeing the [Buddha] beneath the locust tree.
The courtyard is vast on all four sides with no gates; how could one not be moved by the winds of the eight directions?
The Layman of Cangzhou has long admired your reputation, yet he has been unable to join you for conversation. He has sent this letter and bestowed these scrolls upon me.
You must know that what is grasped at hand—does it serve to untie the glue and release the bonds for others? At the crossroads of the street, the staff follows him wherever he goes. For now...
Engaging in the play of the marketplace, after thirty years, pearls and jade shall be of equal value. There must surely be someone who understands this.
Written on the middle day of the waxing moon in the fourth month of the year Jiyou (1249), by Cheng Gongsu of Meishan, as a preface to the first volume of the Recorded Sayings of Master Wumen Kai.
The Discourse Record of Master Wumen Kai, Abbot of Baoyin Chan Temple in Huzhou (Master Yuelin was the founding abbot;
this master was the second generation).
Recorded by Attendant Pujing.
On the ninth day of the fifth month in the eleventh year of the Jiading era, the Master entered the monastery. Pointing to the triple gate, he said: "Father and son do not transmit it;
among a hundred, not one possesses it. Meeting on a narrow path, the door is pushed open and falls into the mortar."
The Buddha Hall: to prostrate is it; not to prostrate is it. "The Yellow-Faced Gautama is beneath my feet. Bottom-line:
mountains encircle the immortal mound, waters wind around the noble tomb. There is resonance within the words; clarity lies beneath the phrases.
The Dharma Seat: one step higher than the last, one stride wider than the last. Turning the pivot at the very top, the entire universe is revealed. Thereupon, he ascended the seat.
Having offered incense to pray for the Emperor, he next held up incense and said: "This incense, if looked upon, causes the eyes to wither;
if smelled, causes the crown of the head to split. Clearly brought forth, I burn it within the burner, to be offered on behalf of..."
He resided twice at Wanshou Monastery in Pingjiang. Later, he took up residence at Wu-hui, where his late teacher, Zen Master Yuelin, was staying.

This was not intended to repay virtue or requite kindness, but rather to engage in a mutual "stalling" (of the Dharma). He then ascended the seat—[the questions and answers are not recorded]—and said:
"In years past, I once went into the mountains; The thousand-armed Great Compassionate One could not block my way. This morning, I have come into the mountains again; The udumbara flower [blooms]..."
Half a day has opened; coming and going are clearly distinct. Today and years past coincide at every turn. Therefore it is said:
"One understands the person of old, but does not understand their former conduct. At such a time as this, tell me:
how do you speak of that single phrase which does not involve coming or going? Sitting upon the *pantala* stone in the deep night, a single incense stick of purity...
Fragrance wafts through the moonlit grove. Again he said: "Residing in thatched huts and grass sheds deep within the mountains, I could not help it when donors came seeking me in vain.
Having settled what my late teacher left unfinished, A foul reputation has since filled the entire forest."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Yunmen, “When the trees wither and the leaves fall, what then?

Yunmen replied, “The essence is revealed by the golden wind. The Master said, “This monk opened his mouth and showed his gall; Yunmen laid bare his heart and liver. I, too, have a verse to present to you all:
When the trees wither and the leaves fall, the essence is revealed by the golden wind. If you ask further ‘What then?’—your eyes are blind and your ears are deaf.”
Ascending the hall, he said: "Observe the news from within stillness; observe from within the midst of clamor. Observe the news from within the midst of clamor; look from within stillness.
Turning over both stillness and clamor, one issues the true command: the long sword leaning against the heavens strikes terror into all who behold it."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: Master Wuzu Yan addressed the assembly, saying: "Autumn clouds and autumn waters, both lingering;
wild geese cry out as they cross the emerald peaks. Most head toward the green grass banks of Lake Dongting; the sky of Chu is so vast and wide that they do not know where to return. The Master said:
"Great assembly, what was the intent behind Grandfather Wuzu’s speaking in this manner? Tell me, what about today at Baoyin?"
Meeting with water and clouds, their sounds resonate with one another—how is this one phrase to be understood? In the end, water must flow toward the sea;
in the final analysis, clouds will surely seek the mountains to return.
The Record of the Tianning Chan Monastery in Longxing Prefecture, compiled by Attendant Pǔtōng.
Three Gates. At the gateway of the bustling marketplace, there is a single phrase: "Waving his hand, he departs the Zhang River; his entire body remains within it."
Buddha Hall. I bow my head to the Elder Gautama. Carrying [the incense] upon my head, I enter the monastery. Having offered incense and performed three prostrations, I ask:

From where do the deities of heaven and earth and the spirits of the human realm come? From what do the sages arise? The five supernormal powers and the six supernormal powers—none of them are it; none of them are it. Today...
How does Tianning instruct? He burns incense and says: "To bring them into alignment, one uses the rites.

The Abbot takes up his staff and says: "In the midst of the bustling marketplace and the red dust of the world, he enters the city and extends his hand; yet as soon as there is the slightest involvement of thought, he strikes the back with the staff and drags [the person] away."
Holding up the notice: This is the eye of the Master, the very nose of Gautama. It is not a four-six prose composition, nor is it benevolence, righteousness, propriety, or wisdom.
I invite everyone to listen with ears pricked.
The Dharma seat is level with the great earth yet rises high above the void; Śākyamuni and Maitreya alike stand beneath its shadow.

Having ascended the seat and offered prayers for the Emperor, [he paused for] questions and answers (not recorded). He then said: "At the crossroads and in the villages of three households, one seeks stillness amidst the clamor and steals moments of leisure in the midst of busyness.
Before the Le-xiu Pavilion, green bamboos draw in the pure breeze; beneath the Tengwang Pavilion, the long river flows on."
Immersed in the bright moon. If you can understand it in this way, the Buddha-dharma and the worldly dharma are both present before your eyes.
If this is not yet so, then one must laugh at Master Liang of old: once he departed for the Western Mountains, he was heard from no more.
Again, the Vice Minister and Imperial Scholar Wu presented this verse: "The clappers in hand, the mallet in the sleeve; I have won the right to perform once upon the stage. [He] sent it.
To those who say there is no gate through which to enter the Way: pack your bags and go forth from the mountains at once. This mountain monk ventures to offer a verse in response:
The eyes are like nostrils; the mouth is like a mallet. The karmic consciousness is in a frantic rush, beyond calling back. The Southern Ford and Western Mountains have not yet been fully tilled.
"Clad in fur and wearing horns, he has come once more.
He ascended the hall and raised the case of Linji addressing the assembly, saying: "The physical body of the four elements cannot preach the Dharma or hear the Dharma;
the spleen, stomach, liver, and gallbladder cannot preach the Dharma or hear the Dharma; empty space cannot preach the Dharma or hear the Dharma. The Master said: "Linji..."
For the Master to speak in such a manner is very much like chewing food and feeding it to an infant. Nevertheless, tell me:
who is it that understands preaching the Dharma and listening to the Dharma? If you can realize this, your studies as a monk are complete.
If not, you must wait until the future to ask Maitreya.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: On Mount Lingyan they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon; Hanshan compared himself to the moon.

From the Buddhas and patriarchs of the past, all have failed in this matter. Tianning is not like that; I have a verse to present to the assembly: "The earth is dark and the sky is dim, yet one sees it intimately;
Who would be willing to follow shadows and reflections to toy with their vital spirit? Under the old monk’s fist, there is life within death. Buddha and..."
Sentient beings swallow it all in one gulp.
Accepting the invitation of the Yellow Dragon, he ascends the hall and addresses the assembly: "Do not distinguish between the marketplace and the mountains;
look with eyes of stillness amidst bustle and busyness. When both paths of quietude and clamor are utterly extinguished, it is like a pearl rolling smoothly upon a golden platter."
The Discourse Record of Huanglong Chong’en Chan Monastery in Longxing Prefecture.
Compiled by Attendant Pǔtōng. Three Gates. 1.
A Single Point Pierces the Three Barriers. Seizing the path of Jiangxi, even Buddhas and Patriarchs ultimately have no recourse. To—
It all depends entirely on this one step.

As for the Buddha Hall: what is it that is within the hall? Where can thousands and tens of thousands of transformation bodies be sought? Prostrating and burning incense—without investigation, they are naturally shattered.
Holding up the notice: From the brush of the Metropolitan Graduate, wind and thunder roll; the swimming scales have long been left unloosed, their gills scorched.
A few drops of water are stirred from the ink-well, washing the light upon the emerald heights of Mount Mufu.

Ascending the seat, he offered prayers for the Emperor (the exchange of questions and answers is not recorded). He then said: "Meeting conditions, the Way manifests; when clouds follow the dragon, they take their place. Following circumstances, one acts as master;

when the wind follows the tiger, it takes its course. Gathering up the entire earth, there is not an inch of soil left. Mountains topple and oceans overturn as clouds are raised and rain is brought forth.
It reaches the point where the three types of grass and two kinds of trees are all equally moistened by the single rain. At such a time as this, tell me: to whom does the merit belong? One.
"Qi does not speak, yet it contains all forms; where could the myriad spirits go to thank its impartiality?

Again, he raised the public case concerning Master Zhigong, who sent someone to deliver a message to Master Huisi of Mount Nanyue, saying: "Why do you not descend the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?"
The Master said: "When Dashi was questioned by Zhigong, he was immediately unable to respond.
If someone were to ask me today, 'Why do you not go down into the mountains to teach and transform sentient beings? I would simply take up my staff and strike them across the back."
Now tell me: are you the same as the ancients, or are you different?
To the two classes of assembly, [the Master] ascends the hall: There is a Great General who kills across the fields without wielding a single blade;
beneath the mountain of Huanglong, he has pitched a formidable camp. In front, he blocks off the three passes; behind, he lays out deep pitfalls.
Linzhi was appointed as the vanguard, Deshan as the rearguard, Bimozhi as the left wing, and Shigong as the right general.

Since he has secured capable men for the front, rear, left, and right, what need is there to speak of the "Long Snake" or "Supine Moon" formations? There is no need to boast of the *Sanlüe* or *Liutao* treatises.

In the space of a laugh, the mad rebels were scattered like smoke; in the blink of an eye, the demonic armies were utterly destroyed. Even so, nevertheless— (Note: The final phrase "且" (qiě) indicates that the text is incomplete and likely leads into a further discourse or a challenge to the audience.)
"How do you understand the phrase, 'Sitting and attaining great peace'? "Without the need for the power of bows or arrows, the crescent moon rises over the slanting Milky Way.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Śākyamuni’s single pivot at the crown of his head and Bodhidharma’s single transmission—Chong'en does not spare his eyebrows;
he simply speaks it as a single phrase."
Ascending the hall: Today is the fifteenth day of the tenth month. Huanglong has a turning phrase; it is clear and plain, not to be hidden away.
I shall state it directly and forthrightly for you: [囗@力]. "The sweet melon is sweet all the way to the stem; the bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If a person recognizes their own mind, there is not an inch of earth in the great world. When the ancients spoke thus, Huanglong was not like that;
he said: "If a person recognizes their own mind, the great world is entirely earth."

Upon ascending the hall after the construction of the Longevity Stupa and his return to the monastery, [the Master] cited the following: During the Tang dynasty, Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Zhong, “After a hundred years have passed, what will you require?
The National Teacher remained silent for a long while and then asked, “Do you understand? Suzong replied, “I do not understand.
The National Teacher said, “I have a Dharma-heir disciple named Tanyuan who is well-versed in this matter; you may summon him and ask. After the National Teacher had passed away, Emperor Suzong...
The Emperor summoned Dan-yuan and questioned him. Dan-yuan said: "South of Xiang, north of Tan, there is gold filling the entire land;
beneath the shadowless tree, the ships are joined together; upon the lapis lazuli palace, there is no one with knowledge. The Master said:

"Suzong did not forget the entrustment, and the National Teacher did not forget the entrustment. Dan-yuan provided a model and a pattern, leaving nothing hidden. This mountain monk shall now emulate him."
Each time he frowned, he would compose a verse: "South of Xiang and north of Tan, shadows roll in circles; On every side of the eaves and rafters, wind and rain bring the cold.
Protruding from empty space without a seam or crack— Let it be viewed by people for a thousand ages."
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Imperial Birthday: "The golden Buddha does not pass through the incense burner;
the wooden Buddha does not pass through fire; the clay Buddha does not pass through water; the true Buddha sits within the house. Master Zhaozhou spoke thus;
while his words hit the mark and are indeed beautiful, they still lack the final phrase. Today, at Huanglong, we celebrate the Imperial Birthday—tell me, where is that final phrase?
"How about the final line? 'The myriad worlds of the great chiliocosm return to the Imperial transformation; for ten million years, may we pray for the longevity of the Sage's person.
Ascending the hall, he cited Master Fóxìng Tàiyé, who said: "Every five days, one attends to a fixed schedule; there is no Way to be attained."
[The Master] said: "There is no Dharma that can be expounded. It would be better to have one's body shattered into fine dust than to allow the eyes of sentient beings to be blinded.
The Teacher said: "Master Tai speaking in such a manner is very much like a thief whose heart is full of trepidation.
Huanglong, however, was not so. Once every five days he went to meet his appointed deadline; there was a Way to be discussed and a Dharma to be expounded, regardless of [the risk of] being shattered.
His body was like fine dust; he simply intended to blind the eyes of sentient beings.
Entering the hall, he raised the case of Master Niyuan, who addressed the assembly, saying: "The essential meaning of that which comes from the West is not easy to proclaim."
At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the true meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Yuan struck him and said, "What kind of occasion is this for you to put your head out now? The Master remarked, "Master Nanyue Ruyuan’s heart was like that of an overbearing mother;
he knew only that 'beneath a heavy reward, there must be brave men,' yet he failed to realize that he was selling a bright pearl as if it were common beans. If it had been...
Huanglong said: "Even the thistle branches would not reach his mouth; why? A crossbow of a thousand *jin* does not release its trigger for a field mouse.
Entering the hall, he said:
"The sun and moon revolve in cycles—what business is this? Monks, you must take care not to let your eyes grow dull and confused. Even if you were to penetrate through completely..."
Beyond the Sound of Majesty, it falls within my own second gear. Quickly realize it; do not hesitate. Sit and watch as the Master of Spring issues his true decree:
the Great Garuda bird soars once and reaches the Celestial Pond.
The Elder of Shanglan Wuhu arrived; the Master ascended the hall. Solely wielding the single-pointed staff, he manifests the upward-moving pivot.

If you seek realization before this pivot, it is already too late. Meeting face-to-face, who can entrust the matter? Though father and son are close, each remains unaware. He strikes the meditation staff and says:
"Since father and son are close, why are they unaware? He strikes again and says: "Fenglin’s *zhazhi*!"
Master Xie Shanglan, having prepared tea and refreshments, ascended the hall and said: "A single mechanism beyond the ordinary is unfathomable to the myriad spirits;

the supreme point above is difficult for even a thousand eyes to perceive. The green mountains and white clouds are the father; the white clouds and green mountains are the child. It is the second and third months of spring."
The peach and plum trees naturally form their own paths. One laughs until one kills the doubt regarding Lingyun’s words, "I have no doubts.
[He] ascended the hall and said: He cited the case of National Teacher An of Songshan, who, when asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
the National Teacher replied, "Why do you not ask for the meaning of your own self? The monk asked, "What is the meaning of my own self? The National Teacher said:
One should contemplate the subtle function. A monk asked, "What is the subtle function? The National Teacher indicated it by opening and closing his eyes;
the monk attained realization. The Master [Dongshan] commented: "How the Great National Teacher leads people into the weeds! That monk had realized something, yet he has not even dreamed of it.
Today, if someone were to suddenly ask Huanglong, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
A blow across the spine, and then a staff—what need is there to speak of "self," or what need to speak of "function"?
Entering the hall, he overturns the great earth and shatters empty space; he swallows the Buddhas and Patriarchs and treats the ancestral style with contempt.
Do not laugh that Huanglong lacks skill; a smoothing iron and a tea kettle are not the same thing.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In practicing Chan, do not stagnate in the effort of stillness; meeting amidst the clamor is already halfway there.
When neither of the two barriers—stillness nor clamor—is encountered, Zhaozhou hangs his gourd from the eastern wall."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A warning: it harms your virtue; silence truly has merit. Even if the vast ocean were to change, it would never communicate for you.
When the ancients spoke thus, they were much like those who plug their ears while stealing a bell.
Huanglong, unwilling to spare his eyebrows, shall once again provide a footnote for everyone. [He then descended from his seat.]
Master Xie ascended the hall to address the assembly. He cited the case where Śāriputra asked Subhūti:
"When one speaks of the six pāramitās in a dream, is it the same as when awake, or is it different? Subhūti replied: "This meaning is profound and subtle; I cannot explain it.
In the Tuṣita Heaven above, there is the Great Being Maitreya who is well-versed in this meaning. You should go there and ask him. The Master [continued]:
He said, "O Great Assembly! This morning the Great Being personally descended from Tuṣita. Huanglong then raised the previous conversation and questioned him.
The Great Being replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time speak dreams; the six ancestral patriarchs speak dreams; the old monks of the world speak dreams;
even down to the sands of the Ganges of Buddhas and all beings of the four sages and six classes of existence—they are all within a dream speaking a dream."

Furthermore, he spoke in verse: "Cultivating the Brahma-conduct of empty flowers, sitting in meditation at the site of enlightenment where the moon reflects in water, subduing the demonic armies within a mirror, and accomplishing the Buddha-work within a dream.
Although it is thus, Huanglong nevertheless has a single flavor of white stone tea;
if the Buddhas of the three periods were to get a taste upon their lips, the eyes of the Buddhas of the three periods would open. If the Patriarchs of the six generations...
If they were to moisten their lips, the eyes of the six generations of patriarchs would open.
Even if all the old monks of the world, the sands-of-the-Ganges Buddhas, and the four classes of sages and six classes of beings were to moisten their lips, their eyes would all open.
Not only would their eyes open, but your skulls would be shattered, your entrails would be consumed, and your very eyes would be forced out. Would you not find this most exhilarating?
Ascending the hall: There is no dharma before the eyes; the intent lies right before the eyes. If you can recognize it right now, you are just right for a punch.
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat: In all the Dharma caves and monasteries under heaven, the retreat begins on the first day of the fourth month.
Without a gate, one pursues evil and follows deviance; yet we must emulate the old precedent of Sishin (Sixin), and I shall urge everyone to strike their foreheads against the ground.
The Buddha ascends the hall on his birthday. Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he was already covered in dust; as soon as he descended into the royal palace, defilement permeated his entire being.
Even if his descendants were to possess the waters of the Canglang River, they would not wash him clean until the year of the donkey.
Incense Offering for the Memorial of Master Yue-lin: I am ill-fated and my eyes lack the power of sight; In my confusion, I encountered the deep venom of the South.
A single handful of my entrails is rent asunder; On this day each year, my heart is pierced with grief.
Thanking the new and old officers for ascending the hall: To build a great mansion, one must rely on many materials; to steer a massive ship, one must depend on many hands.
Once the materials are gathered, the great mansion can be completed; when many hands work together, the great ship will surely cross the waters.
This mountain hermit has unworthily occupied the patriarchal seat, and I am deeply grateful that you all have supported me. The old Hui-chao continues the Dharma as it was preserved. Nan-zen.
The Master’s vow remains intact. Arriving here, his advancing is like a fierce dragon finding water; his retreating is like a mighty tiger relying on its mountain.
What is near? What is distant? There is neither new nor old. In every matter, head and tail meet; within this single gate, a harmonious atmosphere pervades.
The three before and the three after—Sun Face, Moon Face. Although it is thus, tell me: how can one avoid the use of weapons?
Regarding the phrase "Sitting and attaining great peace," how would you explain it? "When power is in one's hand for a single day, watch as the edict is carried out.
He ascended the hall on account of a specific matter: "Right and wrong, long and short, are but the wind passing by one's ear; do not seek out differences or similarities therein.
If you wish to remain unmoved by the eight winds, let the ground of your mind be equal to empty space. The Elder Cishou only knows how to go with the flow.
Set the sails. One cannot steer against the wind. Yet with Huanglong it was not so; both "is" and "non-is" have been cast away.
Within "is" and "non-is," you must offer your realization. Why is this so? Time and again black winds toss up great waves, yet never has it been heard that a fishing boat has capsized.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Yunmen addressing the assembly: "I do not ask about the period before the fifteenth day;
tell me a single phrase for the period after the fifteenth day. Yunmen, acting as his own representative, said: "Every day is a good day. The Master remarked: "This lame-legged fellow!
At first he made such a proclamation, and one might have thought him quite capable; yet in the end, he reveals his true tail—it was all along just that."
"Come, come! Huanglong does not say it this way. Before the fifteenth day, I shall not ask;
after the fifteenth day, bring me a single phrase! With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and said, "The sword has long since departed."
Huanglong ascended the hall at his estate. Huanglong possesses an estate where those who have visited it know its location even before it is mentioned;
for those who have not yet visited it, I shall today describe its appearance so that everyone may understand it thoroughly.
To the east it reaches Pūrvavideha; to the west it reaches Aparagoyānī; to the south it reaches Jambudvīpa; and to the north it reaches Uttarakuru.
Beyond. Within this interval, there is a mountain of priceless jewels heaped up like peaks.
Plowing in spring, sowing in summer, harvesting in autumn, and storing in winter—gathering the entire world back in, opening it wide with eight characters, and bestowing it according to the Dharma.
May each and every person be fully satisfied, leaving nothing lacking. Even so, whether it be a thousand grains, ten thousand grains, or tens of millions of grains, they all proceed from this.
A single grain emerges. If you know the source from which this single grain emerges, you will have cause for lifelong celebration.
If this is not yet the case, you must personally arrive at that very spot before you can succeed.
Ascending the hall to honor the Tripitaka: Gaudama has left behind a tangle of vines; turning them over and examining them, there are many points of liberation.
It is not that his descendants have failed to scrutinize them; how could they fail to resolve the contradictions of past and present?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Studying Chan requires sincerity; one must go directly to the ground of non-doubt. Hearing 'it is not' does not necessarily mean it is not;
hearing 'it is' does not necessarily mean it is. Huanglong established the Three Barriers, and Caodong set forth the Five Ranks. To sit and cut off the Host, one must not fall into the secondary."
Ascending the hall: To follow rules and guard against shortcomings is to bind oneself without ropes. To be unimpeded in movement is to be an outsider among the armies of Māra.

To maintain a mind of tranquil stillness is the heterodox meditation of silent illumination. To abandon conditions at will is a deep pit of liberation. To be alert and unconfused is to wear shackles and carry a yoke.
To contemplate good and contemplate evil is hell and heaven. To perceive Buddhas and perceive dharmas is the pair of Iron Ring Mountains. When thought arises—
One immediately perceives this as the antics of a spirit that toys with the vital essence; it is the ghostly livelihood of those who sit in a state of blank, mechanical concentration.

To advance is to lose sight of the principle; to retreat is to deviate from the core teaching. To neither advance nor retreat is to be a living corpse. Tell me, how ultimately should one tread this path? Exert yourself now;
you must bring this to completion in this very life, lest you suffer eternal immersion in the depths for ages to come.
The Record of the Abbot of Lingyan Xianqin Chongbao Chan Temple in Pingjiang Prefecture, compiled by Attendant Liaoxin.
A blazing conflagration reaches to the heavens; a surging tide rolls to the bottom. The eyebrows are shorn; the sword has long since departed.
Ascending the seat, he offered prayers for the Emperor. (The exchange of questions and answers is not recorded. He then said: "The Buddhas appearing in the world are already established cases;
the Patriarchs coming from the West stir up waves where there is no wind. The 'Four Sevens' and 'Two Threes' speak of yellow and black paths, yet they are seen to be utterly irrelevant.
Today, I, Opening (Kai), shall attempt to sweep them all away with total sincerity. After a long silence, he said: "Even though one’s responsibility is great, one must still follow the ground."
Rising, he said: "How can one contend with the heavens? Again, Master Faden addressed the assembly regarding a case left unresolved by his former teacher.
The Master said: "The eyes look to the southeast, but the mind is set on the northwest. This was not without reason for Faden;
yet that monk was like thorns in soft mud—what was intended as kindness turned into resentment, and both remained unresolved. Today, suddenly there is someone...
He asked Lingyan, "The former master has a case that was not yet resolved; how have you settled it? Lingyan replied to him, "I have no such leisure.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Chan Master Ji of Songshan. Once, a monk asked him, "What is a person of great cultivation? Ji carried [the staff]...
"Chained, bound, and locked. How is it that one who performs great deeds [is thus]? He practices meditation and enters samādhi.
The Master said, "Chan Master Ji, boasting of yourself as such a skilled hand, you have unwittingly fallen into a heavy siege. This monk’s daytime ascension is truly a cause for celebration!"
Today, someone suddenly asked Lingyan, "What is a person of great cultivation? I simply told him: "The accomplished person is not at ease.
He asked, "What is a person of great activity? I simply told him: "At ease, one does not become a person.
If he were to ask how to explain it beyond these two paths, I would simply tell him: "Sulū sulū."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an old case: A monk asked Baizhao, "What are the myriad practices? Zhao said, "This year there are not even peach pits; what need is there to speak of rotten apricots?
The monk asked again, "What is wondrous enlightenment? Zhao said, "If it were a wondrous medicine, I would show you one dose.
The monk said, "I am not asking about this. Zhao said, "What are you asking about? The monk said, "Wondrous enlightenment. Zhao said, "If..."
He gave the soap pods to the bath attendant. The Master said, "Tell me, where does Baizhang’s intention lie?

He ascended the hall and said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure. The spring light has fully leaked forth—whom can recognize the news of spring?
The many-year-old withered tree sprouts branches once more, shaking the spring breeze throughout the eight directions. He struck his staff once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Two-thirds of one's life have already passed. The ox of Huai Prefecture eats the grain; the single point of the numinous terrace has not been polished.
